version.changelog:
- Initial release of UPLO Education skill for academic institutions.
- Enables unified search across curriculum documents, student records frameworks, accreditation data, and institutional research.
- Role-based access ensures users see information relevant to their institutional responsibilities.
- Provides workflows for accreditation evidence assembly and curriculum revision.
- Includes tools for structured search, flagging outdated documents, and proposing updates.

llm.summary: This is a coherent UPLO education knowledge-base integration, but it should be installed only with approved endpoints and scoped credentials because it can access sensitive institutional data.

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose, education knowledge search and accreditation/curriculum workflows, matches the UPLO MCP capabilities and examples. The domain can include FERPA-sensitive and confidential institutional information, so deployment controls are important.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions stay focused on education records, curriculum, accreditation, institutional research, and policy lookup. They also tell the agent to respect classification tiers and avoid fabricating information.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The manifest and README disclose an MCP setup using npx, @agentdocs1/mcp-server, a configured UPLO instance URL, and a secret MCP token. The npm package is not version-pinned, and live package provenance could not be verified in this restricted environment.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: A remote UPLO URL and API token are proportionate for an organizational knowledge-base integration. The artifacts show the URL and token configuration, but users should ensure the endpoint is trusted and uses HTTPS.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The artifact contains only markdown and JSON, with no local persistence, background worker, filesystem indexing, or destructive behavior. Some documented MCP tools can mark entries outdated, propose updates, report gaps, or log conversation context, so write-back tools should be limited to authorized users.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install this only for your institution's approved UPLO instance. Use a scoped MCP token, confirm HTTPS endpoint ownership, and make sure FERPA/classification controls and any write-back tools such as flag_outdated or propose_update are governed by your normal authorization and audit process.
llm.findings: [SQP-2] expected: The secret API token and remote MCP endpoint are expected for this UPLO integration and are visible in the manifest and README. The concern is best handled as installation guidance: use approved HTTPS endpoints and least-privilege tokens, especially because education records may be sensitive.
